newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa wheat crop forecast revised up slightly.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa wheat crop forecast revised up slightly.

text.p: The National Crop Estimates Committee said on Thursday it had raised its estimate of South African wheat production in 1996/97 to 2.593 million tonnes from 2.562 million forecast a month ago.
The committee said the estimated area under wheat remained around 1.293 million hectares from 1.36 million last season.

The comittee said the 30,000 tonne increase in the wheat crop estimate came on the back of an expected higher yield in the Western Cape province's Swartland area where the crop estimate was raised to 735,000 tonnes from 700,000.
The Western Cape is South Africa's major wheat belt.

However, the estimate in Mpumalanga province was decreased to 70,000 tonnes from 75,000 due to damage caused by excessive rain. The committee said further damage could occur depending on rainfall in the next few weeks.

Excessive rain and hailstorms had also caused damage to crops in the eastern Free State, although information on the extent of the damage was not yet available. Further details would be released at the next committee meeting on January 20.

The barley crop estimate had been drastically reduced from 210,000 tonnes to 176,000 tonnes after rain during harvesting in the western part of the production area caused severe damage. The committee said the damage caused by drought in the eastern part had also been more severe than anticipated.
